items.title: Hotspots, peat fires and palm oil: Why tracing Malaysia’s haze is so complicated
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 20 — The return of the haze across parts of Malaysia has once again brought forest and land fires in the region into focus. Malaysia’s response this time includes an offer of firefighting assistance to Indonesia, which reflects the fact that the haze does not stop at national borders. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi on Thursday said Malaysia had offered a Bombardier CL-415MP aircraft, three helicopters and 52 officers and personnel from the National Disaster Management Agency, Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) and the Royal Malaysian Air Force.

items.title: 'Very caring, soft-spoken': Yasin opens up on prison interactions with Najib
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Singer and composer Muhammad Yasin Sulaiman has recalled former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak as a gentleman during their time together at Kajang Prison. Yasin said he got to know Najib while performing at prison events, where the former prime minister was often invited to dine with other guests. Yasin said Najib also took an interest in his case and asked about it several times.

items.title: California takes aim at billionaires with proposed 5pct wealth tax
items.summary: NEW YORK: No state may be a more natural fit for a tax on billionaires than California. But the November 3 ballot initiative Proposition 40, which asks Californians whether to impose a one-time 5 per cent tax on the state's billionaires, is far from certain to pass, political analysts say, amid a debate that has raised questions about income inequality and the state's future business prospects. "Billionaires are no longer very popular," said University of California, Berkeley economics professor Emmanuel Saez, a researcher of wealth inequality who helped write Proposition 40.

items.title: Sri Lanka sends monks skyward to summon rain amid severe drought
items.summary: COLOMBO: Sri Lanka's Air Force said on Sunday it had flown Buddhist monks who prayed and sprinkled holy water over drought-hit areas in an attempt to encourage rain. Sri Lanka's meteorology department has warned that both severe drought and heavy rains are likely to hit Sri Lanka during the rest of the year as the largely agricultural nation faces its "worst" El Nino climate phenomenon. An air force official told AFP the monks were flown aboard a Y-12 fixed-wing aircraft.

items.title: Man held after Chinese tourist allegedly assaulted in resort room
items.summary: Semporna district police chief Superintendent Tan Hiap Wah said the incident was believed to have occurred about 3am while the 25-year-old woman was sleeping in her room. Tan said, acting on information and preliminary investigations, a team from the Semporna district police headquarters Criminal Investigation Division arrested the 18-year-old suspect about 8pm yesterday at the resort. "The suspect was taken to the Semporna district police headquarters to assist in the investigation.

items.title: US warns Mideast war could 'escalate rapidly' after Riyadh missile attack
items.summary: RIYADH: The United States warned that fighting between Saudi Arabia and Iran-backed Houthis could "escalate rapidly" after a missile attack targeted Riyadh for the first time since the Yemen conflict resumed. The White House gave no explanation for the early return, which comes as a new threshold was crossed in the conflict between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis, who control a large part of Yemen and are fighting government forces backed by a coalition led by Riyadh. The United States, according to US news platform Axios, last week refused a Saudi request to strike the Houthis, but Washington has since approved a US$24.3 billion sale of 48 F-35 fighter jets.

items.title: Anwar: Najib has right to seek pardon, but wider impact must be considered
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 20 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has defended former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s right to seek a pardon, while cautioning that its impact on public confidence and international perceptions must also be weighed. Anwar also rejected suggestions that he had paved the way for Najib’s conditional pardon, saying every prisoner had the right to submit an appeal for consideration. “What I said is that every prisoner has the right to submit an appeal, and I stand by defending that right for anyone, including Datuk Seri Najib.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Sunday, September 20, 2026
items.summary: MISSED what happened today? Here's a glimpse at what happened throughout the country in photographs. [[nid:1537060]] [[nid:1537059]] [[nid:1537058]] [[nid:1537057]] [[nid:1537056]] [[nid:1537055]] © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Iran tells US reopening Hormuz hinges on war ending, funds release
items.summary: TEHERAN: Iran's top negotiator said Sunday that Teheran had conveyed to Washington through mediators its conditions for reopening the strategic Strait of Hormuz, which it has blockaded throughout the Middle East war. Mohsen Rezaei, the head of Iran's supreme national security council, said on Saturday that the Islamic republic had conveyed its conditions to the US via mediator Qatar. Iranian authorities have said that mediator Pakistan's Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi will travel to Teheran on Sunday for talks.

items.title: KL, Labuan and nine states under thunderstorm, heavy rain warning
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm, heavy rain and strong wind warning for Kuala Lumpur, Labuan and nine states until 9pm today. In a statement, MetMalaysia said the states involved are Perak, Kelantan, Terengganu, Pahang, Selangor, Negri Sembilan, Johor, Sarawak and Sabah. In Perak, the warning covers Hulu Perak, Selama, Larut Matang, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang, Muallim, Bagan Datuk, Hilir Perak, Perak Tengah and Manjung.

items.title: Tengku Zafrul: Childcare providers key to strengthening family economy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Childcare providers play a vital role in supporting the family economy by enabling parents to work while ensuring their children are properly cared for, said Prime Minister's Senior political adviser Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Tengku Abdul Aziz. He said trusted childcare providers gave parents greater peace of mind while ensuring their children received proper care, making the sector an important part of the country's economic and social support ecosystem. Since its launch in August 2025, Kasih Madani has reached more than 1,000 childcare providers in Kuala Lumpur, Perak, Kedah and Penang through programmes such as the Madani Childcare Pilot Course (Karisma), Madani Childcare Seminar (Semai) and Madani Childcare Professionalisation Skills Mentoring (Bitara).

items.title: [UPDATED] Preliminary report on Felda management due next week
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: A preliminary report on the management of the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) is expected to be ready next week, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said the government was spending RM980 million a year to cover Felda's losses. "Next week, we will receive the preliminary report on Felda.

items.title: [UPDATED] Anwar: Najib's pardon within his rights, other cases to proceed
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Datuk Seri Najib Razak's conditional pardon does not affect other legal proceedings against him, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Anwar said every prisoner had the right to submit a pardon petition, with the decision ultimately resting with the Yang di-Pertuan Agong. Anwar said the advice he had given to the Yang di-Pertuan Agong on Najib's pardon petition did not point towards the decision that was made.

items.title: Anwar to meet Loke before deciding on resignation, says no letter submitted yet
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he will meet Transport Minister Anthony Loke to hear his views before deciding whether to accept his resignation. Anwar said Loke had informed him of his intention to step down following the conditional pardon granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak but had yet to submit a formal resignation letter. Speaking to media in Shah Alam today, Anwar said he wanted to sit down with Loke before making any decision.

items.title: Retired teacher hands over ATM cards, wife's gold necklace in RM15k scam
items.summary: KOTA BHARU: A 75-year-old retired teacher in Bachok lost about RM15,000 after falling victim to a scam syndicate posing as police officers and handing over two ATM cards and his wife's gold necklace with a pendant. Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said police arrested a 31-year-old woman in Kota Baru on Sept 13 to assist in the investigation. He said the incident began on Sept 12 when the victim received a call from an individual claiming to be a police officer from the Johor contingent police Headquarters.

items.title: Childcare is economic infrastructure, not ‘just a job’, says Tengku Zafrul
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — The childcare profession should be regarded as an important component in supporting the family economy and not merely as a job involving the care of children, said the Prime Minister’s Senior Political Adviser Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Tengku Abdul Aziz. He said having trusted childcare providers enabled parents to work with greater peace of mind while ensuring that their children received proper care, making the childcare sector part of the country’s economic and social support ecosystem. Since its launch in August 2025, Kasih Madani has reached more than 1,000 childcare providers in four states — Kuala Lumpur, Perak, Kedah and Penang — through programmes such as the Madani Childcare Pilot Course (KARISMA), Madani Childcare Seminar (SEMAI) and Madani Childcare Professionalisation Skills Mentoring (BITARA).

items.title: [UPDATED] Anwar to meet Loke over resignation
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim will meet Anthony Loke to discuss the latter's resignation from the Cabinet. Anwar said Loke had informed him of the matter, but they had yet to discuss it further. Asked when he would meet Loke, Anwar said Loke might travel to Shanghai, China, first.

items.title: Israel prevent over 100 Palestinian teachers from reaching schools in West Bank
items.summary: RAMALLAH: The Israeli army has closed two checkpoints in the northern West Bank, preventing more than 100 Palestinian teachers from reaching schools, an education official said Sunday, Anadolu Ajansi reported. The Israeli army closed the two checkpoints as part of broader military restrictions across the occupied West Bank. Meanwhile, Israeli forces raided the village of Al-Mughayyir, east of Ramallah in the central West Bank, closed its main entrance and arrested dozens of Palestinians, according to local sources.

items.title: Fake cops scare retired Bachok teacher into handing over ATM cards and wife’s gold necklace
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 20 — A 75-year-old retired teacher in Bachok lost about RM15,000 after being duped by a scam syndicate posing as police officers, which also resulted in the victim handing over two ATM cards and his wife’s gold necklace with a pendant. Kelantan Police Chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said that the police arrested a 31-year-old woman on September 13 around Kota Bharu to assist with the investigation of the case. He said the incident began on September 12 when the victim received a phone call from an individual claiming to be a police officer from the Johor Contingent Police Headquarters (IPK).

items.title: Haze tightens its grip: 32 areas now recording unhealthy API readings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — Thirty-two areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 4.30pm today, according to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal. Other areas with unhealthy API readings included Putrajaya (161), Nilai, Negeri Sembilan (160), Shah Alam, Selangor (157), Seremban, Negeri Sembilan (156), and three areas in Johor - Segamat (156), Batu Pahat and Tangkak (155 each). Other affected areas were Batu Muda, Kuala Lumpur (147), Banting, Selangor (132), Port Dickson, Negeri Sembilan (126), Alor Gajah, Melaka (119), Indera Mahkota Kuantan, Pahang (111), Kuala Selangor (108), Klang (107) and Balok Baru Kuantan in Pahang (103).

items.title: Najib faces continued legal battles despite house arrest
items.summary: The decision by the Federal Territories Pardons Board last Friday allows Najib to serve the remainder of his six-year sentence for the SRC International Sdn Bhd case under house arrest, subject to payment of a RM50 million fine and compliance with the conditions imposed. Najib is appealing the conviction and sentence, with the 15-year sentence scheduled to begin after he completes his SRC International sentence. "If the house arrest period ends in 2028, this means Najib would have completed his sentence for the SRC International case.

items.title: Caught red-handed: Man arrested after woman spots phone filming her in store toilet
items.summary: JERANTUT: A 26-year-old woman realised she was being filmed on a mobile phone while using the women's toilet at a convenience store in Bandar Inderapura here yesterday. Jerantut district police chief Superintendent Nor Azman Yusof said the victim, in her report, claimed she saw someone in the adjacent toilet filming her with a mobile phone over the top of the toilet partition. "The victim's husband also contacted the Jerantut district police headquarters operations room for assistance.

items.title: Man, woman found dead in car had previously planned to marry
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH: A man and woman found dead in a car here early today had previously been close to getting married before ending their relationship, according to the woman's family. The woman's 31-year-old brother said his sister had told the family that her relationship with the 34-year-old man had ended some time ago. I asked a resident, who told me that the man, known as 'Pandan', had died inside the car with a woman," he said.

items.title: Leo XIV, first US pope transcends his restrained style
items.summary: PRUDENT yet conciliatory, Pope Leo XIV has gradually imprinted his style on the leadership of the Catholic Church, finding his voice as he takes on some of the world's most pressing issues, from bloody conflicts to artificial intelligence. When elected to lead the world's 1.4 billion Catholics on May 8, 2025, the former Robert Francis Prevost from Chicago had on-the-ground experience from more than two decades as a missionary in Peru, as well as insider knowledge of the Vatican and Roman Curia. In the nearly year and a half since, Leo's character and priorities have more clearly emerged, revealing a pope unafraid to intercede in some of society's thorniest problems – whether trying to steer emerging technology in a more responsible direction, or exhorting leaders not to write off society's most disadvantaged.

items.title: 27 areas nationwide record unhealthy API readings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Twenty-seven areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as at 4pm today. In Johor, Segamat (156), Batu Pahat (155), Tangkak (155) and Larkin (152) recorded unhealthy readings. In Melaka, Bukit Rambai (153), Bandaraya Melaka (152) and Alor Gajah (119) also recorded unhealthy readings.

items.title: Police: Foreign man who caused disturbance at KLIA suspected of having mental health issues
items.summary: SEPANG, Sept 20 — A Bangladeshi man who behaved aggressively and disturbed passengers at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1 on Thursday is suspected of having mental health issues. KLIA district police chief ACP M. Ravi said the man had shouted loudly and disturbed passengers at an airline counter at KLIA Terminal 1 at 4.40pm. “Terminal security personnel who arrived to bring the situation under control took the suspect to the Terminal 1 police station for further action.

items.title: PKR Youth dismisses calls for Parliament dissolution after Loke's offer to resign
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: PKR Youth has rejected calls to dissolve Parliament following Transport Minister Anthony Loke's offer to resign, stating that government stability is determined by the confidence of the majority in the Dewan Rakyat. Its vice-chief Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari said calls by certain quarters for Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to dissolve Parliament did not reflect the current standing of the government. The unity government continues to hold that mandate.

items.title: Cop’s knock wakes startled Audi driver before wrong-way scare in Johor Bahru
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 20 — A video posted on social media showing a car being driven against traffic on Jalan Jim Quee here has been traced to an Audi driver who is believed to have fallen asleep after finishing work. The knock woke the driver, Ng related, adding that the former then slowly moved the car forward into traffic. But possibly disoriented, the Audi driver was travelling against the flow of traffic towards Jalan Jim Quee.

items.title: Diana's brother compares media treatment of Harry, Meghan to late princess' ordeal
items.summary: LONDON: The media's treatment of Prince Harry and his wife Meghan is on a par with that faced by his mother Diana, the late princess' brother said in an interview published on Sunday, warning that lessons needed to be learned from that period. "If you look at an article in a tabloid about Diana or the couple that you were mentioning, Harry and Meghan, you know, they can be really, really unpleasant," Diana's brother, Earl Charles Spencer, told the BBC. "And I think it would be really beholden on people to learn from Diana's example.

items.title: Indonesia rescue agency recovers another victim from capsized ship
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia's search and rescue agency said on Sunday it had recovered one more victim from the wreck of a passenger ship that capsized and sank in the Java Sea last weekend. "The victim was found by divers during a search inside the ship's hull," the agency said, adding that the victim will be airlifted out for identification. The search and evacuation operation will be continued using divers and also air support, the agency said.

items.title: Missing woman among two found dead in car in Durian Tunggal
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH, Sept 20 — A man and a woman were found dead in a car at Taman Inang Sari, Durian Tunggal here around midnight last night. Alor Gajah district police chief Supt Ahmad Abu Bakar said the bodies of the duo, aged 31 and 33, were discovered at 12.05am. “Initial checks found that the woman was the individual reported missing, while the man was believed to be her acquaintance,” he said.

items.title: Najib house arrest decision first of its kind in Malaysia, says lawyer
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The conditional pardon granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest is the first case of its kind in Malaysia, says a prominent lawyer. However, he said the current situation differs because the Pardons Board's decision specifically involves serving the remaining sentence under house arrest. Sivananthan said the implementation of the decision raises key operational questions, particularly regarding the monitoring mechanism and who will oversee Najib throughout his house arrest.

items.title: Brother recounts failed attempt to pull mother to safety as grilles trap victims in Tambun fire
items.summary: Raja Ikhwan Hadi Raja Ahmad, 47, said his younger brother, Raja Muhammad Shukri, 30, had managed to reach their mother’s hand and tried to pull her to safety, but the grilles prevented him from getting her out of the house. The fire claimed the lives of their elderly parents, Zaitun Mohamed, 64, and Raja Ahmad Raja Ali, 70, as well as their nephew, Nik Abdurrahman Azimin Harith Helal, 18, in the two-storey terraced house at Persiaran Desa Tambun 4, Taman Desa Tambun here. An elderly couple and their grandson were killed in a fire involving a two‑storey terraced house at Persiaran Desa Tambun 4, Taman Desa Tambun in Ipoh early this morning.

items.title: 15 motorcyclists arrested for reckless riding on Lekas
items.summary: KAJANG: Police arrested 15 motorcyclists for reckless and dangerous riding during an operation targeting illegal street racing along the Kajang-Seremban Expressway (Lekas) early today. District police chief Assistant Commissioner Naazron Abdul Yusof said the five-hour Op Samseng Jalanan began at 12.01am. He said police inspected 90 people and 70 motorcycles during the operation.

items.title: China's August oil imports from Russia rise as Middle East flows slump
items.summary: BEIJING: China's crude oil imports from Russia stood at 11.2 million metric tons in August, or 2.64 million barrels per day (bpd), up 41 per cent from a year earlier and 23 per cent from July. Imports from Malaysia, the largest transshipment hub for sanctioned Iranian oil, reached 2.6 million tons, or 620,000 bpd, down 45 per cent year on year but up 74 per cent from July. Imports from Indonesia stood at 3.1 million tons, or 730,000 bpd, up 16 per cent year on year and flat with July.

items.title: Najib touched by RM50mil fund support, says daughter [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: "Daddy really did not expect so many people to be willing to contribute," said Nooryana Najwa Najib, referring to efforts to raise money to pay her father's RM50 million fine. Nooryana said her father expressed how touched he was when she and her family visited the former prime minister at Kajang Prison yesterday. She said he repeatedly expressed how touched he was to see people willing to contribute.

items.title: National Welfare Foundation aid presented to family of late flight nurse Debra Moset
items.summary: KUCHING: The National Welfare Foundation (YKN) has presented immediate disaster relief aid to the family of the late Debra Moset, a flight nurse who died in a Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, on Sept 8. The aid was presented by Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri during a visit to the family's home in Kampung Semadang, Padawan, today. "Peka YKN assistance is an early form of support for victims' families.

items.title: Sungai Gurun breaches danger level, flash floods hit 2 villages
items.summary: YAN: Sungai Gurun in Kampung Perupok here breached the danger level following more than two hours of heavy rain today. The rise in water levels caused flash floods in Kampung Teroi Bukit and Kampung Titi Teras following the overflow of the river. Yan Civil Defence District Officer Lieutenant (PA) Zul Izzi Zulkifli said 11 houses in Kampung Teroi Bukit and eight in Kampung Titi Teras had been affected by floodwaters so far.

items.title: Trial begins for 14 men in Kelantan cross-dressing case [WATCH]
items.summary: KOTA BARU: The trial of 14 men accused of wearing women's clothing and acting like women began here today, with an enforcement officer taking the stand. Lawyer Muhammad Syarafi Mohd Salleh said four enforcement officers involved in the operation were expected to testify. The 14 men were charged at the same court in December last year with wearing women's clothing and shoes and acting like women at the multipurpose hall of Troika Residency, Jalan Sultan Ibrahim, at 11pm on May 30, 2025.

items.title: PM channels RM5,000 initial assistance to Tambun fire victims
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 20 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today contributed RM5,000 in initial assistance to the family of the victims of a fire that claimed the lives of three family members at Persiaran Desa Tambun 4, Taman Desa Tambun, here early this morning. The contribution was presented by Tambun Member of Parliament’s (MP) special officer Mohamad Hairul Amir Sabri, representing the Tambun MP’s Service Centre, to the family’s representative, Raja Ikhwan Hadi Raja Ahmad. Mohamad Hairul Amir said the assistance was an initial contribution to ease the burden on the family, which is now coping with the loss of three family members in the tragedy.

items.title: North Korea fires ballistic missile off east coast, Seoul says
items.summary: South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said it detected the test firing from the Wonsan area around 3pm (0600 GMT), identifying the weapon as a ballistic missile. Japan's defence ministry also said it appeared to be a ballistic missile. South Korea's National Security Council condemned the short-range missile launch, which follows a test on Sept 12.

items.title: Technician killed after car skids into opposite lane and hits motorcycle in Dungun
items.summary: DUNGUN, Sept 20 — A technician was killed after the motorcycle he was riding was hit by a car that lost control at Kilometre 70 of Jalan Jerangau-Jabor near Bukit Besi here this morning. Dungun police chief Supt Nik Ab Halim Nik Mat said the 7.30 am incident involved Mohd Yusop Abu Bakar, 34, who worked at a factory in Bukit Besi and was riding a Honda AFS110 motorcycle from Dungun towards Jerangau. “Initial investigations found that upon reaching the location, a Perodua Myvi driven by a 42-year-old man is believed to have lost control, skidded into the opposite lane and collided with the front of the victim’s motorcycle.

items.title: Malaysia to follow UN decision on any Malbatt deployment to Yemen, says defence minister
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 20 — Malaysia will be guided by any decision made by the United Nations (UN) should there be a proposal to deploy the Malaysian Battalion (Malbatt) peacekeeping force to Yemen amid the ongoing conflict there, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said. Mohamed Khaled, who is also Kota Tinggi MP, said Malaysia would not make such a decision unilaterally, stressing that any action must be based on a UN decision. “Malaysia’s decision will be guided by the decision made by the UN, rather than us acting on our own.

items.title: Fahmi: State‑specific political shifts may lead to Pakatan realignments, cooperation with Bersatu not discussed
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, Sept 20 — The current political dynamics could lead to various political realignments, taking into account the unique political landscape of each state. Pakatan Harapan (PH) communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said recent political developments could not be viewed through a single mould, as each state had its own unique political landscape and dynamics. He said this after officiating the Kampung Angkat Madani (Madani Adopted Village) 2025 initiative of the Communications Ministry at Surau Kampung Tebat Kering, Kuala Pilah, here.

items.title: Floods: Five relief centres opened in Gua Musang, 221 evacuees housed
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 20 — Five temporary relief centres (PPS) have been opened in Gua Musang following heavy rain since last night, with 221 victims from 57 families housed at the centres as of 1.33pm today. The five relief centres are Masjid Jeram Tekoh, Jeram Tekoh Zone 3 Community Hall, Sekolah Kebangsaan Jeram Tekoh, Felda Chiku 6 Community Hall and Sekolah Kebangsaan Limau Kasturi 1. Meanwhile, Kelantan Civil Defence Force (APM) deputy director Lt Col Mohd Farid Ishak said the Gua Musang district APM had deployed personnel in two main teams to carry out follow-up operations in the affected areas.

items.title: ‘Whether Najib is released or not is a separate issue’: Khaled Nordin says King’s pardon prerogative should not be questioned
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 20 — Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin today said any displeasure over former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s conditional pardon should not extend to questioning the Yang di-Pertuan Agong’s constitutional prerogative to grant them. Khaled said the granting of pardons was not unprecedented, with such decisions having been made in numerous cases involving individuals sentenced to death or life imprisonment, while the issue should also not be linked to ongoing efforts to unite Malay political parties. Khaled, who is also Kota Tinggi MP, said efforts towards Malay political unity were focused on safeguarding the community’s interests and political standing, and had nothing to do with Najib’s pardon.

items.title: ‘Lots of noise, then silence’: PAS’ Sanusi questions DAP’s Anthony Loke’s resignation offer over Najib house arrest
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — PAS election director Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor today described the DAP’s decision to have only its secretary-general Anthony Loke offer to resign from the Cabinet over former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s conditional pardon as “firecracker politics”. Loke offered to resign as Transport Minister yesterday after a three-hour DAP central executive committee meeting, while the party decided its other ministers and deputy ministers would remain in the unity government to maintain political stability. “DAP plays flip-flop politics.

items.title: DAP sec-gen’s Cabinet quit offer over Najib house arrest is his own call, says Umno veep Khaled Nordin
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 20 — Anthony Loke’s offer to resign as Transport Minister following former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s conditional pardon is entirely his own matter, Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said today. Loke offered to resign yesterday after DAP’s central executive committee meeting, saying the move was the party’s response to the decision allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest, while other DAP ministers would remain in the unity government to maintain political stability. Khaled, who is also defence minister, said Loke’s resignation offer should not be confused with the decision involving Najib.

items.title: Sentul OCPD: Police to deploy mobile station near Najib’s Langgak Duta residence from tomorrow; Prisons Dept to handle monitoring
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — A mobile police station will be deployed near a former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s official residence in Langgak Duta here from tomorrow to facilitate security arrangements during any transfer from prison to the residence. Sentul district police chief ACP Anuar Bakri Abdul Salam said the mobile police station was scheduled to be deployed at the residence from 7am tomorrow. “The mobile police station is not for the purpose of providing 24-hour security for Datuk Seri Najib.

items.title: MEF: RM1,000 Socso mobility allowance to improve job matching for workers relocating over 100km
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — The one-off RM1,000 Mobility Assistance Allowance for eligible Social Security Organisation (Socso) contributors is expected to improve the matching of workers with job opportunities, particularly where vacancies are located beyond their immediate areas. Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) Senior Adviser for Government, Media and International Engagement Datuk Dr Syed Hussain Syed Husman said the initiative recognised that relocation and extended travel could involve significant upfront costs for workers to take jobs farther from home. However, Syed Hussain said MEF encouraged Socso to clearly communicate the eligibility criteria, application procedures and payment timelines to workers and employers.

items.title: Prisons Dept says still waiting for official notice before Najib’s house arrest can start
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s move from prison to house arrest has yet to get the formal green light from the Malaysian Prisons Department, which says it is still waiting for official written notification of the conditional pardon granted to the former prime minister. The Federal Territories Pardons Board granted Najib a conditional pardon on Friday, allowing him to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to conditions including payment of a RM50 million fine. “Any notification and official documents relating to the Pardons Board’s decision will be conveyed through the appropriate official channels before being submitted to the Malaysian Prisons Department for further action,” the department said in a statement today.

items.title: Education Ministry to revisit 2006 tuition centre ownership provisions, proposal goes to Cabinet next week
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 20 — The Education Ministry (MOE) will submit a proposal to review the ownership structure of tuition centres for Cabinet consideration next week. In a statement today, MOE said the provisions on tuition centre ownership were detailed in the Private Educational Institutions Policy Book published in 2006. “MOE takes note of the various views raised regarding the provisions and is always open to hearing the views of all parties.

items.title: Sarawak agrees in principle to RM1.5b allocation for Sibu Economic Zone, deputy premier says
items.summary: SIBU, Sept 20 — The Sarawak government has agreed in principle to an initial RM1.5 billion allocation to establish the Sibu Economic Zone (SEZ) as a dedicated platform to coordinate and shape the city’s economic development. Also present was ACCCIS president Kong Chiong Ung. Dr Sim said ACCCIS and its affiliated chambers had over the years provided an important platform for business networking, policy dialogue, capacity building and engagement between the government and business community.

items.title: No one should feel obliged to help pay RM50m fine, Najib tells supporters as Umno solidarity fund hits RM1m
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak says Malaysians who have offered to help pay the RM50 million fine required under his conditional royal pardon should not feel “burdened or obliged” to do so. The statement from his lawyers comes as the Najib Razak Solidarity Fund set up by Umno to help him meet the payment reached RM1 million by 9.30am yesterday, less than a day after it was launched. Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the fund collected RM165,645 within its first hour and RM634,562.02 within three hours, with many contributors giving RM10 or RM50.

items.title: Saifuddin Nasution: Proposed House Arrest Act focuses on remand detainees and prison overcrowding
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — The proposed House Arrest Act is aimed at addressing prison overcrowding, particularly involving remand detainees, who make up a significant proportion of the prison population while awaiting trial. Previously, I mooted introducing one specifically for remand detainees, as remand detainees are one of the causes of prison overcrowding,” he said in a video uploaded on his Facebook page today. “So, this combination of convicted inmates and remand detainees contributes to prison overcrowding.

items.title: Frozen assets may hinder RM50m payment for Najib’s house arrest, his lawyers say
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s ability to pay the RM50 million fine required for his house arrest could be complicated by frozen assets, bank accounts and properties subject to government enforcement proceedings, according to his lawyers. The legal firm Messrs Shafee & Co said a “significant part” of Najib’s assets remained subject to freezing orders and enforcement proceedings, meaning their disposal was not presently within his sole control. Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said yesterday that Najib must first pay the RM50 million fine at the Kuala Lumpur High Court Registrar’s Office before the house-arrest process can proceed.

items.title: Perak Fire Dept: Tambun house blaze leaves three family members dead, one injured
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 20 — An elderly couple and their grandson were killed in a fire involving a two-storey terraced house at Persiaran Desa Tambun 4, Taman Desa Tambun here early this morning. Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director Datuk Sayani Saidon said the department received a call at 4 am before a team from the Tambun and Ipoh Fire and Rescue Stations rushed to the scene. Sayani said the 70-year-old male victim was found in the bathroom on the ground floor of the house, while the other two victims were found on the upper floor.

items.title: Haze: Sarawak areas dominate unhealthy API readings, IPD Serian highest at 182
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — Twenty-two areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 9am today. Five areas in Johor also recorded unhealthy API readings, with Larkin recording 162, Batu Pahat and Pasir Gudang 155 each, followed by Segamat (154) and Tangkak (153). Meanwhile, 40 areas recorded moderate readings, while five areas recorded good readings.

items.title: Fire razes 10‑door longhouse in remote Penan settlement in Ulu Baram
items.summary: MIRI, Sept 20 — A 10-door longhouse in Kampung Long Jekitan, Ulu Baram, Marudi was completely destroyed in a fire yesterday. The Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department (Bomba) operation control centre said a distress call was received at about 2.50pm, following which the Marudi Police Station was immediately alerted. It said initial information received indicated that the 10-door longhouse, which was a non-permanent structure, was completely destroyed by fire.

items.title: Rescued Croatian hiker fined RM25,000 over Mount Kinabalu climb says trespassing was ‘last thing on my mind’
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 20 — Croatian hiker Mauro Persic, who was fined RM25,000 for trespassing into Kinabalu Park, has denied deliberately entering the mountain without permission or trying to avoid paying the entry fee. The 46-year-old, who lives in London, said his climb was spontaneous and driven by his desire to explore Mount Kinabalu after seeing its beauty firsthand. I never meant any disrespect to people, culture nor mountain,” he said.
